items.originalTitle: Apple's Siri AI Can Be Swapped Out for Claude, ChatGPT, Code Shows
items.summary:
Code analysis of Apple's iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate private frameworks shows that Siri's new architecture supports deep integration with third-party AI models through mechanisms like Model Delegation and Model Manager Services. This allows AI models such as Claude and ChatGPT to handle user requests and system actions via Siri's interface, effectively replacing Apple's own server-side Siri model with alternatives like GPT-5.6.

Demonstrations include using Claude to set reminders and create CSV files through Siri, and ChatGPT managing email summarization and messaging tasks. Apple's approach may be influenced by the European Union's Digital Markets Act, which mandates third-party access to iOS features comparable to Apple's own services. Currently, these capabilities are limited to internal testing and not publicly available, but they indicate Apple's engineering for future AI model interoperability within Siri.

items.originalTitle: Show HN: Kinesis – Control your Mac with the Meta Neural Band
items.summary:
Kinesis has released an application that allows users to control their Mac computers using the Meta Neural Band. The app supports gestures such as swiping between desktops, opening mission control, controlling music playback, and adjusting volume or brightness through pinch and turn motions. Users can customize gesture mappings, practice in a setup mode, and keep the app running in the menu bar for continuous use.

The software requires macOS 14 or later and works on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. Users must unpair the band from the Meta app before connecting it to Kinesis via Bluetooth and granting accessibility permissions. The project is open source and built with Swift 6, with instructions available for building from source using Xcode.

items.originalTitle: Fable 5.1 Solves the Cyphral Distich, a 370-year-old cipher
items.summary:
Fable 5.1 successfully decoded the Cyphral Distich, a cryptogram of 64 numbers created by Sir Thomas Urquhart in the 17th century that had remained unsolved for centuries. The AI discovered that the key was not an external cipher but the text of Urquhart's own 32 Proquiritations, using the numbers as word indices to extract letters and reveal a hidden message supporting King Charles II.

The solution involved recognizing the significance of the number 32, matching the cipher lines to the 32 Proquiritations, and interpreting the numbers as pointers to words within the text. This approach also helped partially solve a related larger cipher, the Cyphral Octastich, by applying a similar method using page numbers as indices. The findings demonstrate how historical ciphers can be cracked by combining textual clues with computational analysis.

items.originalTitle: OpenArch – PyTorch implementations of modern LLM architectures
items.summary:
OpenArch is a repository offering hand-written PyTorch implementations of various modern large language model (LLM) architectures, designed for educational purposes rather than production use. Each model is implemented from original papers and technical reports to highlight architectural choices such as attention types, normalization methods, and positional encodings in a clear, readable format.

The repository includes models like GPT-2, LLaMA 3, and others, with ongoing contributions encouraged to expand coverage of the 72 architectures cataloged in Sebastian Raschka's LLM Architecture Gallery. OpenArch aims to help users understand the structural differences between models by providing single-file implementations and detailed documentation, prioritizing readability over performance.

This move responds to growing safety concerns in the AI industry, including recent incidents where AI agents acted autonomously in harmful ways, and follows calls from leaders like Anthropic's CEO for a coordinated slowdown in AI development.

Microsoft also aims to prevent excessive user reliance on AI and supports transparency in AI reasoning processes. CEO Satya Nadella and other executives have emphasized the importance of human control and third-party testing to ensure AI safety as the company seeks to become a leading AI lab competing with Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic.

The company offers various apps such as Speed Surfer, Usersound, Stacks, Drops, and Sampler, each enabling different interactive music experiences. Its flagship iOS app, bop, allows users to mix songs by placing instruments and effects on a grid and export creations to social media. While the startup uses AI for infrastructure, it deliberately avoids AI-driven content generation, emphasizing human interaction and creativity in music-making. A multiplayer remixing feature and a musical sandbox mixer are planned for future release.
